calls.head: Who blinks first?
calls.body: The Oilers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years. The Panthers take a lot of penalties, so the Oilers’ power play should get its chances.

calls.head: Like for like: Schwindt vs. Joseph
calls.body: At home, the Panthers keep sending Schwindt’s line (Imama, Schwindt and Hathaway) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Paul Maurice keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Oilers’ fourth line is Formenton, Michaels and Joseph.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Podkolzin has two goals and an assist as the Oilers beat the Panthers
paras: Kasperi Kapanen opened the scoring for the Oilers midway through the first, and Connor McDavid made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. Vasily Podkolzin stretched the lead to 3-0 midway through the second, and he scored again on the power play later in the period to make it 4-0. Matthew Tkachuk scored with just over six minutes left and again just under three minutes later to cut Edmonton’s lead to 4-2. Leon Draisaitl added an empty-net goal with 33 seconds left to make it 5-2. Three players had three-point nights: Draisaitl with a goal and two assists, Kapanen with a goal and two assists, and Podkolzin with two goals and an assist.

The Oilers had the better of the chances. Devon Levi made 20 saves for the Oilers, and Jacob Markström stopped 13 of 17 at the other end. Levi has won six straight starts. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Evan Bouchard, by our Swing measure.

The Panthers killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes midway through the third. The Oilers improved to 17-3-3, still first in the NHL in points, while the Cats fell to 12-8-3, fifth in the Atlantic.

items.text: Connor McDavid has a point in all 23 games this season.
Leon Draisaitl tied Mark Messier for third on the Oilers’ all-time assists list, with 642.
The Oilers are rolling: six straight wins.
All three of the preview’s calls held.
